calendar_note: Year A. Spring 1 Week 5, 1–5 February 2027. Tuesday 2 February 2027, P3. One 40-minute preparation and recording lesson for up to five learners. Source F + S retained as mixed evidence role; Week 6 assesses the term. Spring 1 runs 4 January–12 February, six weeks. Actual encounter date recorded separately; no clock time supplied.
source_adaptation: E20 weekly outcome, F20 focus, G20 lesson outcome and J20 evidence retained exactly. H20 sequence retains questions on course content, entry, support, travel and progression, two-way interaction and suitability reflection. I20 is an encounter window, not fixed phases: the 5/8/10/12/5 split adapts it to the requested 40-minute lesson. School arranges the actual encounter and separate duration/timing/entitlement checks. Staff role-play is labelled practice and does not establish a real encounter occurred. Real encounter, staff role-play and pending records remain distinct. Review and preferences private; K20 websites replaced by in-pack cards, normal aids and reduced choices retained.

sources.note: Physical row 20 is Spring 1 row 5. E20, F20, G20, J20 and N20 verified exactly. H20 sequence retained. I20 encounter window adapted to a 40-minute preparation/recording lesson; school owns separate encounter arrangements. Prepared generic scripts replace website research when needed. Raw workbook not distributed.
Accepted BUILD Week 4 supplies clean layout, folder shape, generic picture bank and retrieval continuity. This lesson uses row 20 outcomes and evidence with an explicit encounter-window adaptation.

Tuesday 2 February 2027 P3. Exact outcome. School-arranged encounter; prepare and record with date, category only, question, answer and yes/maybe/no. Staff plays invented provider if visitor absent. No named provider, college, training organisation, person or place. Same BUILD rules. Next Week 6 assessing, one per return; further GROW Careers paused. Pause for Downloaded.

routes.Supported: Choose between two ready questions. Keep the picture, question card, model and word bank. Rehearse privately. Use speech, sign, aid, typing or an adult voicing the learner’s selected question. Exact scribe reads back. Record help supplied.
routes.Independent: Choose a ready question or build one from a topic. Ask through the usual communication mode, record the answer and yes/maybe/no reflection. Keep normal reading and communication aids.
routes.Aspire: Ask a relevant follow-up or identify a fact still to check. Link the reflection to one answer feature. No extra public presentation or personal disclosure required.

cases.intro: I am playing a made-up college provider. This is practice, not a real place or offer. Ask me a question about this option.
answers: You would try short lessons and guided practical tasks.
We would talk about what you can do and check the needs of the course. No place is promised.
You could ask for a word card, a short break or help with a step.
The place and journey are not set in this practice card. Ask a trusted adult to help check travel before a real choice.
You could look at another course or training. You would need to check its entry needs.
cases.followup: Which word or part would you like me to explain?
cases.boundary: I do not have that fact on this practice card. Let us record it as a question to check.

cases.intro: I am playing a made-up training provider. This is practice, not a real place or offer. Ask me a question about this option.
answers: You would learn job skills in a small group and try guided tasks. This card does not offer a paid job.
We would discuss your starting skills and check what the training needs. No place is promised.
You could ask for a short task list, a model or help to read a step.
No real journey is given here. Check the route, time and help with a trusted adult before a real choice.
You could explore more training or a job with training. You would need to check the next entry needs.
cases.followup: Would you like a shorter answer or an example?
cases.boundary: I do not have that fact on this practice card. Let us record it as a question to check.

colour_blind_safe: Pictures, captions and words carry meaning; no colour-only codes.
worked_examples_status: All worked examples, provider scripts and model reflections are invented and generic. Pictures are symbols, not real people or places. Actual learner questions, answers and preferences must be recorded honestly. No named provider, college, organisation, person, place, product or platform.
private_help_route: Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write or ask for a private talk. Pass, pause and supported return are available. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. No real grades, home address, travel history or family finances requested.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Either question choice uses Evidence Sheet page 2, Type instead, with blank fields. Save through usual routine with lesson code/work reference; show adult privately. Exact scribe records words/selections, reads back and permits correction. Record usual access separately from supplied content.
worked_example_and_fade: A mentions word cards and short breaks. Which question fits? A what help could I ask for; B what is the journey time? Key A. Point to the answer clue if unsure. Keep the question bank and usual aids; fade only answer cues.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: five short topics, two question choices, model and chunked recording. Communication and Interaction: pre-teach words, rehearsal, frames, processing time and usual aid. SEMH: predictable turns, private choice, pass, pause/return; no public questioning. Sensory and Physical: clear pictures/text, seated or quiet access and no colour-only codes. EAL: plan in any language and rehearse question meaning.
misconceptions: A provider category is not one named organisation. A training option does not always include a paid job. A promising answer does not guarantee a place. Maybe is a valid reflection; an unknown stays unknown. Practice scripts do not describe actual provision.

main_hinge.claim: Record unknown travel honestly and ask for help to check.

parallel_hinge.claim: Ask again about unclear entry details and note the unknown.

success: Ask a prepared question in the usual communication mode.
Record actual answer or unknown with date, mode and category only.
Record yes/maybe/no privately and identify a feature heard; preference ungraded, personal reason optional.

evidence.description: Provider encounter record and suitability reflection. Keep actual date, mode, category, question, answer, feature, yes/maybe/no, unknowns, access, prompts, first response, NS and reply.

assessment: Exact source evidence: Provider encounter record and suitability reflection. Keep actual date, mode, provider category only, prepared question, asking mode, actual answer, yes/maybe/no, a feature heard, optional reason, unknowns, access, prompts, first response, one NS and reply. A chosen question voiced by an adult can be aided asking; log it. A question supplied without learner selection is not independent preparation. Preference is never graded. Keep partial evidence; pass unobserved.

encounter_boundary: School arranges the real encounter and checks its required duration, timing and entitlement records separately. This 40-minute lesson and staff role-play do not establish completion of a real provider encounter. If the visit happens elsewhere, use this lesson to prepare and complete the record at reflection. Never claim a visitor attended when absent. Use a separate dated record for each mode; leave future answers pending. No names in this pack or shared records.

preference_policy.pending_rule: If encounter not yet happened, leave answer and preference pending. Pass is unobserved; do not choose for learner.

paragraphs_in_document_order: Tuesday 2 February 2027 · P3 · 40 minutes · Year A
Careers · BUILD · up to five learners · Spring 1 Week 5
Theme: Resilience & Change. Source N20 is F + S: formative preparation and retained encounter evidence. Week 6 is the assessing week.
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C: none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T: none).
Students meet a provider and explore what it is like to learn or train in a different setting.
I can ask a prepared question and record whether the option could suit me.
Focus: Provider encounter 2 — FE/ITP and progression
Source: BUILD Careers physical row 20 / Spring 1 row 5, E20–N20.

Prepare and ask a useful question, listen to the answer and make a tentative private reflection. FE means further education; ITP means independent training provider. These are categories, not names. Progression means a possible next step. Yes, maybe and no are all valid preferences; no place or final decision is promised.

Ask a prepared question using the usual communication mode. Keep the actual answer or an honest unknown. Record yes/maybe/no and identify one feature heard; a reason may remain private. Judge the question and record, never the preference.

Confirm school-arranged encounter, category, access and private question turns. If no visitor, select script A or B for staff role-play. Books, question cards, record and usual aids ready. Keep provider/person/place names out of shared work. No internet, login or phone. Confirm trusted adult and pause/return.
This helps me ask about learning or training and decide what I need to find out next.
Recall a Week 4 question to check or supply a model; unknown facts can be asked about.
Pre-teach provider words; model a prepared question, answer and tentative reflection.
Choose a topic, plan and rehearse a question; check how to record an unknown answer.
Use the arranged encounter or an honestly labelled staff role-play; ask, listen and record.
Privately record yes/maybe/no, one feature and any next question; bank actual evidence.

5 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 40 minutes. This lesson split is an adaptation: I20 describes an encounter window, not fixed phase minutes. Slides 7 and 8 share 23–35 minutes. Processing and brief pauses included.

0–5: recall a Week 4 fact to check; supply the idea if absent. 5–9: read exact outcome and explain provider categories, question, answer and progression. 9–13: model asking the support question to invented A, hearing word card/break/step help, recording the answer and choosing maybe while another fact remains unknown. The model is not a required learner answer.

13–19: use planning Card 1. Choose ready question or build one about course content, entry, support, travel or progression. Rehearse privately with a partner or adult; no cold calling. 19–23: hinge on an unanswered travel question; model an honest note and next check. Keep each learner’s prepared question.

23–35: use private or quiet turns with the arranged visitor, or staff playing invented A/B. Learner asks by voice, aid, typed message or chosen card voiced by an adult. Respond to that question, then allow a clarification. Others rehearse or record while waiting. Keep actual question and answer; read back for confirmation. Record mode and actual date. Do not prefill a visitor answer from the script.

35–38: record yes/maybe/no, a feature heard and an optional reason in private; mark unanswered facts honestly. Set one NS and retain reply. 38–40: show prepared question and reflection, then bank the record. If the real encounter is later, keep its date/answer/reflection pending; any practice has its own role-play label.

Choose between two ready questions. Keep the picture, question card, model and word bank. Rehearse privately. Use speech, sign, aid, typing or an adult voicing the learner’s selected question. Exact scribe reads back. Record help supplied.
Choose a ready question or build one from a topic. Ask through the usual communication mode, record the answer and yes/maybe/no reflection. Keep normal reading and communication aids.
Ask a relevant follow-up or identify a fact still to check. Link the reflection to one answer feature. No extra public presentation or personal disclosure required.

A mentions word cards and short breaks. Which question fits? A what help could I ask for; B what is the journey time? Key A. Point to the answer clue if unsure. Keep the question bank and usual aids; fade only answer cues.

Main: travel details are not known. A invent a journey time; B write not known yet and ask for help to check. Key B. Re-model fact versus guess. Parallel: an entry answer is unclear. A ask for it again and note what is still unknown; B write any grade. Key A. Recheck privately; pass is unobserved.

Cognition and Learning: five short topics, two question choices, model and chunked recording. Communication and Interaction: pre-teach words, rehearsal, frames, processing time and usual aid. SEMH: predictable turns, private choice, pass, pause/return; no public questioning. Sensory and Physical: clear pictures/text, seated or quiet access and no colour-only codes. EAL: plan in any language and rehearse question meaning.

Prompt ladder: 1 point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 provide scaffold/choice; 5 model first step only, then return task. I Do: show question and answer. We Do: prompt topic choice. You Do: support the learner’s question and record actual words without supplying a preference.

Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write or ask for a private talk. Pass, pause and supported return are available. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. No real grades, home address, travel history or family finances requested.

Either question choice uses Evidence Sheet page 2, Type instead, with blank fields. Save through usual routine with lesson code/work reference; show adult privately. Exact scribe records words/selections, reads back and permits correction. Record usual access separately from supplied content.

Exact source evidence: Provider encounter record and suitability reflection. Keep actual date, mode, provider category only, prepared question, asking mode, actual answer, yes/maybe/no, a feature heard, optional reason, unknowns, access, prompts, first response, one NS and reply. A chosen question voiced by an adult can be aided asking; log it. A question supplied without learner selection is not independent preparation. Preference is never graded. Keep partial evidence; pass unobserved.

A provider category is not one named organisation. A training option does not always include a paid job. A promising answer does not guarantee a place. Maybe is a valid reflection; an unknown stays unknown. Practice scripts do not describe actual provision.

One NS can make a question clearer or separate an answer from a guess. VF verbal feedback; WS worked with support; I independent; // self-edit; ? read back; E actual banked evidence. R follows Voice, Audience, NS and reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. Offer to Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping.

School arranges the real encounter and checks its required duration, timing and entitlement records separately. This 40-minute lesson and staff role-play do not establish completion of a real provider encounter. If the visit happens elsewhere, use this lesson to prepare and complete the record at reflection. Never claim a visitor attended when absent. Use a separate dated record for each mode; leave future answers pending. No names in this pack or shared records.

H20 topics, two-way questions and suitability reflection retained. I20 encounter-window note acknowledged; phase split adapted. Script fallback provides responsive staff practice, not an actual provider visit. No live research. Next BUILD Week 6, My route map — Plan A and Plan B, assessing; then previously queued LAUNCH Careers Week 1. Further GROW Careers paused. Only Week 5 authored.

Theme: Resilience & Change. Source F + S; mixed evidence role. Week 6 assessing.
Students meet a provider and explore what it is like to learn or train in a different setting.
I can ask a prepared question and record whether the option could suit me.

5 retrieval + 8 I Do + 10 We Do + 12 You Do + 5 review/exit. Phase split adapts I20 encounter window. Prepare a question, rehearse, ask and record through the school-arranged encounter or clearly labelled staff role-play; private reflection.

Ready question or build one. Five topics; reduced two-choice scaffold, model, pictures and usual aid. Book, typed record or exact scribe. Private turns, no cold calling. Trusted adult/help route, pass and pause/return.
Provider encounter record and suitability reflection.

Record actual date, mode, category only, question, answer and yes/maybe/no; one feature heard and optional private reason. Keep unknowns, access, prompts, NS/reply. Bank in Careers Portfolio; offer to Communication portfolio. Pending encounters stay pending.
This helps me ask about learning or training and decide what I need to find out next.
BUILD Careers physical row 20 / Spring 1 row 5, E20–N20. Tuesday 2 February 2027 P3. No named provider or person. Staff fallback is practice only. Next BUILD Week 6 after Downloaded.
Get one question ready. Use your book, point, type or use your aid. An adult can read or write your words.
Pick a ready question on Card 1, or build one from a topic. Practise it with an adult. You do not need to speak to the whole group.
Ask the question in your usual way. An adult may voice the card you choose. Listen to the answer. You can ask, “Please say that again.”
Write the date and provider type. Add your question and the answer. Mark real encounter, staff role-play or pending. Use a new record for each talk. No names.
Choose yes, maybe or no in private. All three are fine. Show one thing you heard. You may add, “It might suit me because ... .” You do not have to share a private reason.
If you do not know, write “not known yet”. Keep one next question. Do not make up an answer. If a visit is still to come, leave its answer and choice pending.
Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP or ask for a private talk. You may pass, pause and return. Keep private worries out of this record.
Use one record for each talk. No names. If it has not happened, leave the answer and choice blank. Mark pending.
The answer or not known yet
Could it suit me yes maybe no
My reason if I wish to add one
One next step and my reply
Types: further education college; independent training provider; technical education provider. Record the type given, not a name.
Save in the usual way with the lesson code and work reference. Show an adult privately. A book, aid or exact scribe is also fine.
Keep what was said. Real and practice talks need their own date.
How it was asked and the answer
One fact and yes maybe no choice
First response one NS and reply
Question shown partly shown not seen
Record shown partly shown not seen

No choice is right or wrong. A pass means not seen yet. A staff role-play is practice, not a real visit. E: work saved. R: Voice, Audience, NS and reply. Add to Careers Portfolio. Offer to Communication portfolio.
I can ask a prepared question and record whether the option could suit me.

A prepared question must come from the learner’s choice or construction and be asked through their usual communication mode. Adult voicing of a selected card is valid aided asking; record it. Keep the actual answer or unknown, a feature heard and yes/maybe/no reflection. Preferences are not graded. No compulsory personal explanation.

Model A: support question matches word card, break and step help. Main B: unknown travel stays unknown, with help to check. Parallel A: ask again about unclear entry details and note the unknown. Re-model fact versus guess, then recheck privately. A pass is unobserved.

Course content, entry, support, travel and progression are all valid. A prepared question about any one topic meets the core asking task. A relevant follow-up can deepen it. Do not require all five questions from each learner or rush five public performances.

Use actual visitor answers for a real encounter. The fallback script facts apply only to the labelled role-play. Unknown facts must not be invented. Generalise any provider/person/place names in shared notes to category wording. The typed template stays blank; no supplied model answer is counted as learner evidence.

FE is further education, ITP independent training provider. The categories may overlap in real provision; record the category given rather than forcing a false distinction. Technical education is learning for a type of work. Progression means a possible next step, not a guaranteed place or job.

Content: short lessons and guided practical tasks. Entry: discuss current skills and check course needs; no promised place. Support: word card, short break or step help. Travel: no place/journey set; check with a trusted adult. Progression: another course or training, with entry checks. Exact script replies are on Card 2.

Content: work skills in a small group and guided tasks; no paid job offered by this card. Entry: discuss starting skills and training needs; no promised place. Support: task list, model or reading help. Travel: no real journey; check route/time/help. Progression: more training or a job with training, with entry checks. Exact replies on Card 3.

Staff choose a script, introduce it as invented and wait for the learner’s question. Answer its topic, then offer the listed clarification and allow a response or pass. If a question is outside the card, say the fact is not available and record a next check. Reading a script at learners without their question is not evidence of asking. Rehearsal and aids remain available.

Yes, maybe and no are equally valid. In the model, maybe is linked to word-card help and unknown travel. A learner may choose any option and keep a reason private. Ask them to identify one neutral feature heard; do not ask for diagnoses, grades, addresses or finances. Record a pass or missing reflection honestly, never choose on their behalf.

One NS can sharpen a vague question, retain the actual answer, distinguish unknown from guessed, or name a feature. Keep first response and reply. Do not turn a tentative preference into a commitment or an eligibility judgement.

Exact evidence: Provider encounter record and suitability reflection. Source N20 F + S retained as mixed evidence role; Week 6 assesses the term. Record actual date, mode, category, question, answer, feature, yes/maybe/no, optional reason, unknowns, access, content supplied, NS/reply. A later real encounter requires its own date and record. Preparation alone is not completed encounter evidence.

School owns the real encounter arrangements, duration, access and separate entitlement/timing checks. This lesson or staff role-play does not establish compliance or completion. If the visitor is elsewhere or later, prepare now and record actual answers and reflection when it occurs. A practice record is labelled staff role-play, never visitor attended.

Evidence Sheet page 2 works for either question choice and every mode. Keep names out. Exact scribe reads back and allows correction. Save with usual routine, lesson code/work reference; share privately. No real booking or application is made.

E actual evidence banked; R after Voice, Audience, NS and reply. Add record to Careers Portfolio and offer to Communication portfolio. Staff confirm any accredited mapping. Missing or partial evidence remains visible; no invented answers or attendance.

Trusted adult or school’s help route; point to HELP, write or ask privately. Pass and supported pause/return remain available. No public questioning or personal records. Listen calmly, avoid probing or secrecy promises and follow usual procedures; keep concerns out of shared evidence.
